---
title: "Installation"
---

`{baler}` ships as a native binary. There is no R package to install for the CLI itself, only for the `{box}` fork it depends on at runtime (see [below](#the-box-fork)).

## Pre-built binaries

Pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows are published on the [Releases](https://github.com/joshuamarie/baler/releases) page.

1.  Linux / macOS:

    ``` bash
    curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/joshuamarie/baler/refs/heads/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
    ```

    2.  Windows:
    
    ``` bash
    powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/joshuamarie/baler/refs/heads/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex"
    ```

To pin a specific version, use that version's asset URL instead of the `latest` one the scripts above resolve to:

``` bash
curl -LsSf https://github.com/joshuamarie/baler/releases/download/v0.1.0/baler-installer.sh | bash
```

``` bash
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://github.com/joshuamarie/baler/releases/download/v0.1.0/baler-installer.ps1 | iex"
```

## Building from source

`{baler}` is a CLI tool built in Rust, so it requires the stable Rust toolchain (`rustc`, `cargo`). Once you managed to add the Rust toolchain, install `{baler}` from scratch via following command: 

``` bash
cargo install --git https://github.com/joshuamarie/baler
```

`{baler}`'s GitHub-install path (`baler install gh:user/repo`) is compiled behind the `network` feature on `baler-core`. If you're building from source and plan to install modules directly from GitHub, confirm that feature is enabled for the binary you build, otherwise `baler install gh:...` will fail with an explicit "requires the 'network' feature" error rather than silently doing nothing.

### Verifying the install

``` bash
baler --version
```

## The `{box}` fork

You are working with `{box}` modules, and `{baler}` is the "package manufacturer", so it requires `{box}` R package. `{baler}`-installed modules are resolved through `{box}`, although the syntax and path-resolution patches that make `box::use()` aware of `baler`'s install location aren't in upstream `{box}` yet. Until they land, install the patched fork:

``` r
# install.packages('pak')
pak::pak("joshuamarie/box@feature/baler-support")
```
